data.name: Eleanor 'The Duchess'
data.description: A noblewoman of the colonial salons, witty and cosmopolitan, whose presence at court steadies the governor's cabinet.

data.name: Anne-Sophie de la Croix
data.description: A French-born lady of New Orleans salons, known for her sharp tongue and the chandelier dance she choreographed for the Carnival.

data.name: Carolina de los Reyes
data.description: A creole beauty of the Tierra Firme, legendary for her patronage of poetry and the planters' ball of Cartagena.

data.name: Marie-Madeleine de Plessis
data.description: A widow of the Louisiana frontier, soft-spoken yet cunning, who guides the governor's household with an iron hand.

data.name: Anne Bradstreet
data.description: A Puritan poetess of the Massachusetts colony, whose verses lift the spirits of the Sabbath-keeping towns.

data.name: Sarah Kemble Knight
data.description: A colonial diarist and tavern keeper of Boston, who rode the post-roads alone and traded in land warrants.

data.name: Marie-Rose Durocher
data.description: A Quebecoise seamstress of the Saint Lawrence, who founded a convent and a school of needlework.

data.name: Anne de Montagne
data.description: Daughter of a Huguenot settler of the Hudson valley, learned in the herbs of the New World.

data.name: Charlotte de Savereux
data.description: Mistress of the Bordeaux merchant fleet, a French planter's daughter and sharp-eyed at the customs house.

data.name: Maria de la Garza
data.description: A noblewoman of the Rio Grande, keeper of the Spanish colonial land grants and household shrine.

data.name: Kateri Tekakwitha
data.description: A Mohawk-Algonquin convert of the Mohawk valley, a weaver of beadwork and a lay sister of the Jesuits.

data.name: Nanye-hi
data.description: A Cherokee Beloved Woman of Chota, beloved of the Overhill towns, famous for her counsel at the peace councils.

data.name: Margaret Brent
data.description: A landowner of colonial Maryland, executor of the Calvert estate and a defender of the colony's militia.

data.name: Tituba
data.description: A P Boca islander in the service of the Salem parsonage, versed in folk medicine and the folktales of the Caribbean.

data.name: Eliza Lucas Pinckney
data.description: A South Carolina planter's daughter, who introduced indigo culture to the colonial Lowcountry.

data.name: Catherine de Verdier
data.description: A French Huguenot spinning mistress of the Carolinas, who kept the household and the small silk nurseries.

data.name: Mary Johnson
data.description: An indentured servant of the Virginia tobacco fields, who by thrift and diligence rose to the housekeeper's keys.

data.name: Anneke van Voorthuijsen
data.description: A Dutch widow of New Amsterdam, keeper of the Bowery Lane farm and the orange grove.

data.name: Brita Stina Pipping
data.description: A Finnish wife of the New Sweden colony, builder of the log cabin and the sauna by the Delaware.

data.name: Anna Petrovna Prohorova
data.description: A Russian Siberian cossack's daughter who crossed the strait, a fur-trader and wife of the Kodiak garrison.
